our_view.thesis_status: All four thesis pillars remain intact through the full 6-quarter history reviewed (2025 Q1 through 2026 Q2). Total Leverage Ratio has improved every single quarter since close -- 3.3304x (2025 Q1) -> 2.8972x -> 2.6612x -> 2.5098x -> 2.4235x -> 2.3911x (2026 Q2) -- comfortably inside the 5.50x maximum with a wide and widening cushion (~57% headroom at June 2026), driven by contractual amortization and steady EBITDA growth (TTM Covenant EBITDA $24.5M vs FY2024 UW EBITDA $17.5M). Cash has built every quarter ($27.3M -> $36.4M). Revenue and EBITDA beat the approved budget in 5 of the last 6 quarters; June 2026 is the FIRST quarter with a negative variance (-$59,787.70 revenue, -$85,898.18 EBITDA vs the monthly plan), but both misses are small (<0.5% and <3.7% respectively) and both revenue ($13.16M) and EBITDA ($2.29M) are still up year-over-year (+6.2% and +9.3% vs June 2025). No customer, collections, or covenant stress is evident: AR aging buckets have grown roughly in proportion to revenue with no material bucket-mix deterioration across the months sampled, and no restatement, correction notice, or lender query appears anywhere in the Portfolio Management or Period Archive history (unlike Nemeris's corrected Q2 2026 covenant calc or Asteron's restructuring). This reads as a clean, steadily deleveraging credit; watchlist is off.
our_view.what_would_change_our_mind: A second consecutive quarter of negative budget variance on revenue or EBITDA, a Total Leverage Ratio reversal (an increase quarter-over-quarter rather than the steady decline seen to date), a material AR aging bucket shift toward 61-90/90+ (collections/retainage risk crystallizing), or loss of a top-5 customer/project would move trajectory toward 'stable' or 'deteriorating' and warrant turning the watchlist on.

business.vertical: Infrastructure field services (utility, municipal, and industrial inspection/construction-support/repair/maintenance)
business._archetype_note: JUDGMENT CALL: 'consumer-inventory' clearly does not fit (no consumer/D2C sales). The closer call is 'asset-heavy-industrial' vs 'services-project'. Chose asset-heavy-industrial because the collateral and balance sheet are genuinely EQUIPMENT-led, not just receivables-led: Net Property and Equipment ($53.1M) is ~39% of Total Assets ($134.5M) at June 2026 -- larger than Accounts Receivable ($18.1M) or Inventory ($9.8M) -- and the security agreement pledges 'machinery, vehicles, and equipment' as a named collateral category alongside accounts and inventory (equipment yards in Albany, Syracuse, and Buffalo per the Information Certificate). The IC memo and management presentation also frame the business around 'backlog visibility' and 'crew utilization/materials purchasing/change-order capture' driving margin -- close to asset-heavy-industrial's 'backlog and book-to-bill, margin vs volume (absorption)' KPI emphasis. 'services-project' was the other real candidate (payroll-heavy field crews, project/milestone billing, unbilled-AR dynamics) and would also be defensible; flagging both for the analyst since the memo does not itself use either label and this is a genuinely close call between a construction/field-services contractor (asset-heavy-industrial-ish but not a manufacturer) and a project-services business (services-project-ish but with real owned equipment as collateral, not just cash-flow-based recovery).

facility.draw_structure: Single advance at closing (2025-01-15); no delayed-draw or revolving capacity. Proceeds refinanced legacy debt in full -- no proceeds retained for later borrowing.

transcription_notes: Current-period certificate (2026-06, a quarter-end): 06 Monitoring/Portfolio Management/2026 Q2/Covenant Calculation.xlsx 'Summary' tab reports Total Leverage Ratio 2.3911x vs Maximum 5.5x, Status COMPLIANT, test date 2026-06-30. This ties exactly to 04 Reporting/Period Archive/2026/06/certificate.html, which independently states the same Funded Debt ($58,650,506.80), Trailing Covenant EBITDA ($24,529,022.34), Total Leverage Ratio (2.3911x) and Status (COMPLIANT) for 2026-06-30 -- the certificate.html's own text confirms 'The covenant status below is reported only when a formal quarter-end test is required', and June 2026 is a quarter-end.

Per the run's request to report the full historical trend and cross-check every quarter, all 6 certified quarterly test dates (2025-03-31 through 2026-06-30) were transcribed from each quarter's own Covenant Calculation.xlsx, not only the current period's certificate -- one entry per test date, each citing its own quarter's file in 'section'.

EXCEPTION (recorded for the orchestrator): the certified-values contract's 'source' field names one certificate file, but the borrower's 6 quarterly workpapers are all identically named 'Covenant Calculation.xlsx' in different '<YYYY Qn>' subfolders. 'source' above is set to the CURRENT period's file (2026 Q2); the engine's upstream-document resolution for that file name may therefore land on whichever same-named file its folder search encounters, so the automatically-resolved 'upstream' hyperlink on the five PRIOR quarters' rows may not point at their own quarter's specific file even though this JSON's own 'section' field correctly names it. Alternative reading: split the 5 historical quarters into their own certified-values files (one per quarter) so each gets an unambiguous 'source' -- not done here since the contract's shape is one certified-values file per module run/period, and the per-date 'section' field carries the correct locator regardless.

performance.methodology: Company-prepared/unaudited monthly financials model (read via monitor_lib). EBITDA is the model's single pinned bridge row. Normalized metrics strip config.comparability_items. Ratios are spot on latest-month flows; leverage/coverage are TTM within the current same-basis segment when >=12 such months exist. Standouts, drift, trend and the MoM bridge are objective/mechanical and confined to same-basis segments; the line read covers EVERY IS/BS leaf with rule-based flags (no statistical gating); narrative interpretation is left to synthesis.
